# Correctness and security review, October 2026

Branch `claude/code-security-review`, base `main` at `d8d5c3d` (31 Oct 2026).

**Scope.** The Python pipeline (`fetch_nigeria.py`, `fetch_all.py`, `save_events.py`,
`clean_events.py`, `build_map.py`, `publish.py`, `update_candidates.py`, `settings.py`,
`build_history.py`), the workflows in `.github/workflows/` and `.github/agents/scripts/`.
`map_template.html` and `history/template.html` were read only where pipeline data goes into
HTML. They were not fully audited.

**How it was checked.** I read every file in scope. I ran
`python -m unittest discover -s tests` (125 tests, OK) and
`python -m unittest discover -s .github/agents/tests` (18 tests, OK). Two local experiments
backed specific findings: a two-server redirect test (S1) and `git apply` on a patch that
writes into `.git/` (S9). Nothing called the UCDP API, and there is no token in this
environment. No workflow was run on GitHub. The workflow changes were checked by YAML
parsing and by reading them against GitHub's documentation from memory, so they are
**not verified live**.

Severity: **high** (credential exposure or a path to the live site),
**medium** (a real weakness that needs something else to go wrong first),
**low** (worth fixing), **note** (no action needed, or a decision for you).

Checked and fine: SQL in `clean_events.py`, `build_map.py` and `save_events.py` uses `?`
placeholders for values; only fixed column lists or quoted API field names are formatted
into the SQL (S11). No `${{ github.event.* }}` text from issues or comments goes straight
into a `run:` script: comment bodies, briefs, reasons and branch names all go through
`env:`. `issue_comment` is the only comment trigger, and there is no `pull_request_target`.
The agent jobs have read-only tokens, and the publish jobs (which can write) run no AI and
no code from the branch. All of them refuse branches that do not start with `agent/`.
`publish.py` refuses to write a page that contains the token. Neither `publish.log` (which
goes into the PR body) nor the `fetch_log` table contains the token, and nothing prints
it. Pagination stops at `MAX_REQUESTS` even if `NextPageUrl` loops. Stable and Candidate
date ranges do not overlap: `date_end <= END_DATE` against `> END_DATE`.

---

## S1. The token follows redirects and `NextPageUrl` to any host (high, fixed)

**Where.** `fetch_all.py` followed `data["NextPageUrl"]` and sent `x-ucdp-access-token` to
whatever it said (formerly line 235, then `get_json`). All three scripts used
`urllib.request.urlopen`, and on a redirect it **copies every header, custom ones
included, to the new URL, even another host or plain `http://`**. I checked this locally:
a 302 from server A to server B delivered `x-ucdp-access-token: SECRET` to B
(Python 3.13; the code is the same in 3.12).

**Failure scenario.** UCDP's API or a proxy in front of it sends a redirect, or a
misconfigured `NextPageUrl`, to another host or to `http://`. That could be a migration, a
CDN, a captive portal on a laptop's Wi-Fi, or a compromise. The token is then sent in
clear text or to a third party. In `update.yml` that is the repository secret.

**Fix (done).** `fetch_nigeria.py` now has `is_ucdp_url()` (https,
`ucdpapi.pcr.uu.se`, port 443, no user info) and `open_ucdp()`. `open_ucdp()` refuses any
other URL, and its opener refuses any redirect that leaves the API. `fetch_all.get_json`
and `update_candidates.is_published` use it (two lines changed in `update_candidates.py`),
and `fetch_all` stops if `NextPageUrl` is not a UCDP URL. Tests:
`tests/test_pipeline_safety.py` (`UcdpUrlTests`, `RedirectTests` with real local servers,
`FetchAllTests`).

## S2. Cache poisoning: agent-run code can reach `update.yml` (high, your decision)

**Where.** `update.yml:39-44` restores `data/taswira.db` with `restore-keys: taswira-db-`,
then runs Python with `UCDP_TOKEN` and a `contents: write` token saved in `.git/config`.
Every workflow triggered by `issue_comment` or `schedule` runs against the default branch,
so they all share one cache scope. Untrusted code runs in that scope in two places. The
`checks` job (`agent-task.yml:483`) runs `python3 publish.py`, which imports
agent-written `build_map.py`, `settings.py` and `fetch_nigeria.py` in implement mode. The
Claude job (`agent-claude.yml:101`) gives Claude `Bash(python3:*)`.

**Failure scenario.** A web page or issue comment that the agent reads carries a prompt
injection, and the agent writes code that runs in one of those jobs. GitHub-hosted runners
have passwordless `sudo`. Code with `sudo` can read the runner's own token from memory and
save a cache entry `taswira-db-<anything>`. This is a published technique ("cache
poisoning", e.g. A. Khan's *Cacheract*, 2024). The entry is a tar archive, and
`actions/cache` extracts it with absolute paths allowed. It can therefore drop files
outside `data/`, for example a `sitecustomize.py` in the user site-packages. On the next
Monday, `update.yml` restores it, and the first `python update_candidates.py` runs the
attacker's code with `UCDP_TOKEN` and a token that can push to any branch. If `main` has no
ruleset, that includes `main` and therefore the live site. I have not reproduced this; it
is the documented technique applied to these files.

**Options (for you).**
1. *Recommended:* stop using the shared cache in `update.yml`. Keep the database as an
   **artifact of `update.yml` runs** and download the latest one with
   `gh run download -R … --name taswira-db $(gh run list --workflow update.yml --status success --limit 1 --json databaseId --jq '.[0].databaseId')`.
   Agent workflows cannot upload artifacts to another workflow's runs. Alternatively,
   download everything every week. That costs a few hundred of the 5,000 daily requests
   and about 10 minutes.
2. Remove `sudo` from the Claude job after the apt installs (S3), and do not run
   `publish.py` from the agent branch in `checks`. Or run it in a job that does not
   restore the cache and cannot reach it, but no job on the default branch is fully out of
   reach.
3. In any case: add the ruleset on `main` (`SETUP.md` step 6), so that a stolen
   `contents: write` token cannot publish. Also set `persist-credentials: false` in
   `update.yml` and give `git push` credentials only in the last step (S15).

## S3. The Claude job runs untrusted code with `sudo`, and scrubbing env vars does not protect the secrets (medium, your decision)

**Where.** `agent-claude.yml`. `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB` removes secrets from
the environment of Claude's shell commands. But the job keeps `sudo`; Codex uses
`safety-strategy: drop-sudo` and Claude does not. Implement mode allows
`Bash(python3:*)`, and review mode allows `Bash(curl:*)` (which can write files with `-o`)
plus `Write`/`Edit`. After Claude finishes, the "Package the result" step runs `git add -A`
and `git diff` in the checkout Claude could write to (lines 150-151), and runs
`.github/agents/scripts/agent_task.py` from that same checkout (line 148).

**Failure scenario.** A prompt injection makes Claude do one of two things. It can run
Python that uses `sudo` to read `/proc/<pid>/environ` of the action process, which holds
`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`/`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, then send the token out with `curl`. Or it
can write `.git/config` (`core.fsmonitor`) or a changed `agent_task.py`, which the package
step then runs outside the sandbox. Either way, the worst outcome is a stolen
Claude/Anthropic credential and the S2 chain. Neither can push to `main` directly: the
job's `GITHUB_TOKEN` is read-only, and the publish job checks the patch again. Whether
Claude Code's own sandbox stops `/proc` reads here was **not verified**.

**Options.** After the installs, remove sudo:
`sudo rm -f /etc/sudoers.d/runner && ! sudo -n true`. Test that `claude-code-action` still
works without it. Copy `agent_task.py` to `$RUNNER_TEMP` before Claude runs, and call that
copy in the package step. Run that step's git commands with
`-c core.fsmonitor= -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null`, or build the patch in a fresh job from
an uploaded tarball of the working tree. Consider dropping `Bash(curl:*)` and relying on
`WebFetch`.

## S4. `publish.py | tee` hides a failed publish check (medium, fixed)

**Where.** `update.yml`, step "Download, clean and rebuild". A `run:` step with no
`shell:` uses `bash -e {0}`, without `pipefail` (GitHub documentation; not reproduced
live). The status of `python publish.py | tee publish.log` is therefore `tee`'s.

**Failure scenario.** `publish.py` refuses to write the page because the token is in it,
the credit is missing, or preliminary data is unlabelled. The step still passes, and a pull
request "Add GED Candidate X" opens that changes `settings.py` only, with the old
`docs/index.html`. The reason goes to stderr, so it is not in the PR body. Merging it
records the version as published while the map does not show it.

**Fix (done).** `set -o pipefail` at the top of that step.

## S5. The SVG check can be bypassed (medium, fixed)

**Where.** `build_history.py:77` (formerly 74). Emblem drawings go into
`docs/history.html` as raw SVG through Leaflet `divIcon` `html` (`history/template.html:1255`).
The old pattern `\son\w+\s*=` only caught handlers after whitespace.

**Failure scenario.** `<svg/onload=alert(1)>`, `<svg><animate/onbegin=… attributeName=x>`
and `<svg><set attributeName="onmouseover" to="…">` all passed (checked). Implement-mode
agents may write `history/drawings/*.svg`. If such a drawing passes review, script runs on
the live history page.

**Fix (done).** The new pattern also refuses handlers after `/` or a quote,
`iframe|embed|object|use|image|style`, `javascript:`, and `attributeName` that targets
`on…`/`href`. The current drawing passes, and `build_history.py --check` passes. Tests:
`tests/test_build_history.py::test_drawings_are_plain_shapes`. An allowlist of elements
and attributes would be stronger, and that is worth doing if more drawings are added.

## S6. A fork PR can stop the weekly updates (medium, fixed)

**Where.** `update.yml`, "Skip if a data pull request is already waiting": any open PR
whose head branch starts with `data/ged-` counted.

**Failure scenario.** Anyone forks the public repo and opens a PR from a branch called
`data/ged-x`. Every Monday run then says "waiting for … to be merged" and does nothing,
with no error.

**Fix (done).** The check now ignores PRs from forks (`isCrossRepository`).

## S7. `UCDP_TOKEN` was in the env of every step (low, fixed)

`update.yml` set the token at job level, so `actions/checkout`, `actions/cache`, `gh`
and `git push` all received it. It is now set only on the check step and the
download/publish step (`publish.py` needs it to check that the page does not contain the
token).

## S8. Escaping inside `<script>`, and placeholder replacement (low, fixed)

**Where.** `build_map.py:69` `to_js` only replaced `</`. `fill_template` replaced
placeholders one after another.

**Failure scenario.** A place or group name containing `<!--<script>` puts the HTML
parser into its "double-escaped" script state, so the real `</script>` does not close the
block and the page breaks. A field containing `__UNMAPPED_JSON__` (or `__BOUNDS__`, …)
was replaced in turn, which put raw JSON inside a JavaScript string: the page broke, or
data was injected into the script. The data comes from UCDP over TLS, so this is
robustness more than an attack.

**Fix (done).** `to_js` escapes every `<` as `<`, plus U+2028/2029. `fill()`
replaces all placeholders in one pass. For normal data the output is byte-identical to the
old code (checked against a re-implementation of the old chain). Tests: `PageTests`.

## S9. Agent path check: `.git/` and letter case (low, fixed)

**Where.** `agent_task.py` `check_paths`.

**Failure scenario.** A forged patch that writes `.git/hooks/post-commit` passed
`check_paths`. `git apply` then refused it (`invalid path`, checked), so this was
protected by git rather than by the script. `Docs/index.html`, `.GitHub/…` and
`agents.md` were allowed. On GitHub these do not touch the live site, but on your Windows
checkout they are the same files as the protected ones.

**Fix (done).** Any `.git` path component is refused, and the protected-path comparisons
are case-insensitive. Tests: `Paths.test_case_and_git_folder`.

## S10. Fixed delimiter for multi-line outputs (low, fixed)

`write_output` used the constant `__AGENT_EOF__`. A value with that line in it could end
the output early and set other step outputs. No output written today is both multi-line and
untrusted, but the delimiter is now random (`secrets.token_hex`). Test:
`Outputs.test_multiline_output_cannot_end_early`.

## S11. Save check and quoting of field names (low, fixed)

`save_events.py` refused a download only if `len(events) != TotalCount`. If pages shift
while paging (a release updated mid-download), one event can arrive twice and another be
missing, and the count still matches. `INSERT OR REPLACE` then silently drops the
duplicate and the missing event is lost. `incomplete()` now also requires
`unique ids == TotalCount`. Field names from the API's JSON were wrapped in `"` without
escaping; `quote_name()` now doubles any `"`. Tests: `SaveTests`.

## S12. Forged artifacts within one run (medium, your decision)

Every job in a run can upload artifacts to that run. A compromised Claude job (S3) could
upload `codex-review-1` or `checks` before the real jobs do. The real upload then fails
on the name clash. The publish job would record a fake "no findings" review, or the final
report would show "checks passed" and recommend **approve**. Your merge is still the
gate, but the report would be wrong. Mitigation: S3 (no sudo), and have the publish and
report jobs check the artifact's id and creation time against the producing job (the
`upload-artifact` output `artifact-id`, passed as a job output).

## S13. HTTP 429 is read as "not published" (low, open)

`update_candidates.py:51` treats every 4xx as "this version does not exist". If the daily
limit is used up (429), the Monday run says "No new Candidate release" with no error.
Suggested one-line fix: `if e.code == 429: sys.exit("HTTP 429: the daily request limit is used up; try again after midnight UTC.")`
before the 4xx test. I left this to the session that is changing `update_candidates.py`.

## S14. Fields in `innerHTML` without `esc()` (low, open)

`map_template.html:508,750-753` insert `e.date_start`, `e.date_end`, `e.violence_label`
and the death counts without `esc()`. Today they are safe in practice: `clean_events.py`
casts counts to `int`, the label comes from a fixed dictionary, and dates are the first 10
characters of UCDP's value. But a 10-character date field is not a guarantee. `esc()`
also does not escape `'`; that is fine as long as every attribute uses `"`. Suggest
wrapping those fields in `esc()`. I left this to the session that is changing the
template.

## S15. Pinning and saved credentials (low, your decision)

`claude-code-action` and `codex-action` are pinned by commit. `actions/checkout`,
`setup-python`, `cache`, `upload-artifact` and `download-artifact` are pinned by tag.
These are GitHub's own actions (lower risk), but pinning by commit is the stricter rule.
`update.yml`'s checkout keeps the `contents: write` token in `.git/config` while it runs
Python on restored data (see S2). Suggest `persist-credentials: false` and
`gh auth setup-git` (with `GH_TOKEN`) at the start of the push step. I did not change this
because I could not test the push here.

## S16. Re-runs keep the original actor (note)

`authorize` checks `github.actor`. When someone re-runs a workflow run, `github.actor`
stays the person who triggered it first, and the re-runner is `github.triggering_actor`.
A collaborator with write access could re-run an old task of yours. This only repeats a
brief you already authorized. To close it, also require
`github.triggering_actor == github.actor`.

## S17. Candidate events that are later dropped (note, your decision)

`clean_events.py:122-129` keeps, for each id, the row from the newest Candidate release
that has it. An event that UCDP removed in a later release is still shown from the older
one. Whether that is right depends on whether later monthly releases are meant to replace
earlier ones for the same months. If they are, keep only the newest release that covers
each month.

## S18. The checks job's protected-path list differs from `agent_task.py` (note)

`agent-task.yml:455` checks `.github/ docs/ AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md .env .gitignore`, but
not `.claude/`, `.codex/`, `.gitattributes`, `.gitmodules` or `.mcp.json`. The publish
job's `check-patch` is what actually enforces the rule, so this only affects what the
report says. Suggest calling `agent_task.py check-paths` from the checks job, so there is
one list.

## S19. `build_history.py` replaces one placeholder after another (note)

`build_history.py:1231-1234` replaces `{{DATA}}`, then `{{TRANSCRIPT}}`, then `{{BUILT}}`.
A chapter text containing `{{TRANSCRIPT}}` would have HTML put into the JSON. The data is
written by you and checked into git, so this is a note. The `fill()` approach from S8
would fix it.

## Files changed

- `fetch_nigeria.py`: `is_ucdp_url`, `open_ucdp` and a redirect handler that refuses
  redirects off the UCDP API.
- `fetch_all.py`: uses `open_ucdp`, and stops on a `NextPageUrl` that is not a UCDP URL.
- `update_candidates.py`: two lines, to use `open_ucdp`.
- `save_events.py`: `quote_name`, `incomplete` (unique-id check).
- `build_map.py`: `to_js` escaping, single-pass `fill`.
- `build_history.py`: stricter `UNSAFE_SVG`.
- `.github/agents/scripts/agent_task.py`: `.git` and case-insensitive path rules, random
  output delimiter.
- `.github/workflows/update.yml`: `pipefail`, token only on the two steps that need it,
  fork PRs ignored.
- Tests: `tests/test_pipeline_safety.py` (new), `tests/test_build_history.py`,
  `.github/agents/tests/test_agent_task.py`.

`docs/` and `map_template.html` are unchanged. `publish.py` is unchanged.
